note: From the 2026-08-30 verify pass on the Balearic arbres singulars register, 16 rows within 25 km of Mao. Six trees verified and delivered to data/research/menorca-verified.json: Pi Ver del Doctor Camps, Pi de Cala Galdana, Alzina d'Alfuri de Dalt, the Platers de l'Ermita de Sant Joan des Verger, and both trees of the Illa del Llatzeret (Drago and Pi Felip). Leads failed only our evidence or access bar; blocked can never ship as they stand.

leads.name: Alzina de s'Artiga Vella
leads.why: Register id 403, Alaior. Ownership is Privada/particular, no evidence found this run of a public path or right of way crossing the property. Failed only on access evidence, not on the tree itself; worth a second look if a Cami de Cavalls branch or similar is later found to pass nearby.

leads.name: Pi Ver del Rafal Roig
leads.why: Register id 664, Es Mercadal, beside a stream about 300m off the main road toward Ciutadella. Privada/particular. SDL Medioambiente (2016) independently gives its height as almost 13m and repeats the same Dr Francesc Camps planting story as men_001 (Pi Ver del Doctor Camps), so the two 'pi ver' trees may share an origin. No access evidence found; stays a lead.

leads.name: Alzina Grossa
leads.why: Register id 408, Es Mercadal. Privada/particular, no access evidence found this run.

leads.name: Pacaners de s'Hort Squella
leads.why: Register id 650, Alaior, a pair of pecans, unique in the Balearics, said to have been brought back and planted by Menorcan emigrants returning from Mexico (per the CAIB register's own introductory document and repeated by SDL Medioambiente). A genuinely good story but privately held (particular) with no access evidence found this run; worth chasing if the story alone justifies asking the owner.

leads.name: Alzina de sa Torreta
leads.why: Register id 401, Mao. Privada/particular, no access evidence found this run.

leads.name: Ullastres de s'Aeroport
leads.why: Register ids 681 and 682 (two rows, 300m apart, beside the airport car park), reportedly the oldest, near-millennial specimens on the island per SDL Medioambiente. Privada/particular for both. If they genuinely stand beside the public airport car park (as SDL implies, 'al lado del aparcamiento del aeropuerto') rather than on fenced private land, this deserves a proper access check next pass; would fold the two rows into one entry as twins if confirmed. Not chased further this run to stay inside the time box.

leads.name: Tamarells de l'Illa d'en Colom
leads.why: Register id 678, a grove of 50 tamarisks on the dunes of Illa d'en Colom, planted over 100 years ago, said to be the largest tamarisk grove in the Balearics. Privada/particular per the register. Also fails the collectible-point test as it stands: 50 trees across a dune system is an ensemble/habitat, not a single point to stand at, closer to 'a whole wood' than a destination tree.

blocked.name: Pins de Biniatzem
blocked.reason: Register id 666, Es Migjorn Gran, publicly owned (Consell Insular de Menorca). Confirmed via the CAIB fitxa itself as a roadside alignment of pines on both sides of the Ferreries-Es Migjorn Gran road (the road was split into two carriageways around the trees in 2008); the register's own text says the interest is 'per la disposicio a les dues bandes de la carretera', i.e. the arrangement along the road, not any individual specimen. This is the avenue case CLAUDE.md and BRIEF_RESEARCH.md both name as non-collectible: no single obvious place to stand, 19 of an originally catalogued 27 remain (8 dead), and several show traffic-accident scarring. Never ships as a single entry; if a single outstanding specimen among the 19 is ever singled out with its own coordinate and story, that could be reconsidered.

blocked.name: Alzina de s'Alqueria Blanca
blocked.reason: Register id 402, Ferreries. The register's own notes field says plainly: 'Arbre en regressio, practicament mort' (tree in decline, practically dead). Privately held (particular) as well. Never ships: this project does not publish dead trees, and there is no public-access evidence in any case.

blocked.name: Drago de l'Illa del Llatzeret

location.address: In the garden of the old Lazareto (quarantine station), Illa del Llatzeret, Mao harbour, Menorca

blocked.access: Restricted to guided visits: the island is reached only by a Fundacio Foment del Turisme de Menorca boat tour departing the Calesfonts dock in Es Castell (2.5 hours, runs seasonally, paid ticket, booking required, contact llatzeret@menorca.es); not a walk-up destination
blocked.transport: Guided boat crossing from the Calesfonts dock, Es Castell, roughly 15 minutes from Mao by car to reach the departure point
blocked.verify_notes: CAIB official register fitxa (catalogued 17/02/2003, register id 417/19): stands in the garden of the former Lazareto de Mao, a quarantine station built for ships and travellers arriving from the Indies, historically used to treat infectious disease. A Canary Islands species, documented as planted in 1928 (so a real, sourced planting date for this specimen, not a bridge claim: age given directly as '97 anys, planted 1928' in an apparently later revision of the fitxa, which puts today's age at roughly 98 years). Notable in the Balearics for being one of few large, well-preserved, unmutilated dragon trees that grew in situ. Wide crown with 7 primary branches, 9.4m canopy diameter, only 3.8m tall, base perimeter 3.80m, perimeter at 1.3m 2.50m (girth_cm 250), abundant fruiting, leaves in good condition. Owned by the Ministerio de Sanidad (public). Independent source SDL Medioambiente (2016) repeats the 1928 planting date and location, confirming the register. The island itself is confirmed as a real, bookable public destination via the Consell Insular de Menorca's own tourism page for guided Llatzeret visits (boat from Calesfonts, 2.5-hour tour); exact current pricing was not confirmed on that page directly and is left out rather than guessed. This is a paid, seasonal, guided-only site, which the access field states plainly per hard rule 10's viewing/access tests.
blocked.blocked_reason: Hard rule 10: reachable only on a booked guided boat tour to the Illa del Llatzeret (Fundacio Foment del Turisme de Menorca, 2.5 hours, from the Calesfonts dock at Es Castell). The rule allows paid entry and does not allow an appointment, and a scheduled seasonal tour you must book is an appointment rather than a gate you walk through. Fully verified otherwise, 2026-08-30: the dragon tree has a documented 1928 planting and the Pi Felip carries the register's own 2025 note about a lost branch, which is the freshest proof of life on the whole island. If the island ever opens to independent visitors, or Hidde rules that a booked tour counts, both ship as they stand with no further research.

location.address: In the garden of the old Lazareto (quarantine station), Illa del Llatzeret, Mao harbour, Menorca

blocked.transport: Guided boat crossing from the Calesfonts dock, Es Castell, roughly 15 minutes from Mao by car to reach the departure point
blocked.verify_notes: CAIB official register fitxa (catalogued 17/02/2003, register id 662/55): stands a few metres from the dragon tree in the same Lazareto garden, notable for its unusually wide, flat-branched crown, spreading 20.8 by 26 metres on just four primary branches, height only 10m, trunk diameter 1.14m (base perimeter 440cm, perimeter at 1.3m 360cm, girth_cm 360). Several branches are propped up. The register itself is explicit about declining condition: mature specimen with unbalanced structure, low vitality, high fragility, only 40-60% of canopy volume remaining, and notes it lost another branch as recently as 2025, which is unusually current confirmation that the tree is a living, monitored specimen. Owned by the Ministerio de Sanidad (public). Independent source SDL Medioambiente (2016) corroborates location and species and gives a close height figure (10.5m vs the register's 10m). Same access as the neighbouring dragon tree: paid, seasonal, guided-boat-only visit to the island via the Consell Insular de Menorca's own Llatzeret tour.
